notes: SHIP v1.14.434 - M2-b STAGE 2: THE RECLAIM BARRIER (RACKENGINE-SPEC section 6, invariant I6). No context is acquired in the same task as a release. Not a retry and not a timeout - an ORDERING guarantee. WHAT WAS WRONG, READ FROM THE ORDERING RATHER THAN MEASURED. Both renderers ACQUIRED before they RELEASED. rackElevation_render3D constructed its WebGLRenderer roughly 1200 lines before it called register(), and register() is what runs releaseOthers(); forge3d_render had the same shape. So on a cross-host handoff - Build to Aisle is exactly that shape - the new context was taken while the other host s was still live. I1 held AFTER register ran, never at the instant of acquisition. The invariant the engine claimed was true one line too late. CLAIM DISCIPLINE, RECORDED IN THE CODE AND THE TESTS. The ordering is CERTAIN and is what this ship pins. A field failure caused by it is NOT proven - desktop tolerates two live contexts - and this must not be cited as the explanation for the historical blank-rack arcs. What is fixed is a stated invariant that was not actually being held. THE FIX. releaseOthers now RETURNS the number it released, and both renderers release at the TOP of the function, before any renderer is constructed. When something was actually released the barrier arms: a flag plus a DOUBLE requestAnimationFrame, after which one pending acquisition runs. Deferral re-enters the same function with the same arguments, so the deferred path IS the normal path rather than a second implementation of it - on re-entry there is nothing left to release, the barrier is down, and it proceeds. WHY DOUBLE rAF, from the spec: on iOS WebKit the GPU-side reclaim from forceContextLoss is asynchronous and a single rAF can still land in the same compositor frame. Two frames is about 33ms, imperceptible to a human, and a guarantee rather than a hope. Verified in the harness by counting frames between release and acquisition, not by trusting the call. THE BARRIER ARMS ONLY WHEN A RELEASE ACTUALLY HAPPENED. Arming unconditionally would put two frames in front of every first render on a cold device, waiting for a reclaim that never occurred. That is why releaseOthers had to start reporting a count. ONLY ONE PENDING ACQUISITION IS HELD. Rapid navigation collapses to the LAST request instead of queueing N allocations, and the collapse is counted in the census - queueing them is how one refusal becomes a pile-up. Pinned: three requests behind an armed barrier produce exactly one acquisition, the last. IT CANNOT DEADLOCK. A hidden tab never fires requestAnimationFrame, so _armBarrier falls back to a timer. A barrier that strands the pending work forever is worse than no barrier, and that fallback is pinned by test. TEARDOWN ALREADY RECLAIMED PROPERLY - checked before building on it: the attachment dispose path ends in renderer.dispose() followed by renderer.forceContextLoss(), so the barrier is guarding a real reclaim rather than a bookkeeping change. barrierReport() is a SEPARATE reader rather than a widening of report(): report() returns the attachment array that several specs and callers already consume, and one reader deserves one shape. TESTS: new spec 23-reclaim-barrier, seven tests - a cold acquisition proceeds immediately, an armed one is deferred and then runs on its own, three requests collapse to the last with the collapse counted, the gap is at least TWO frames measured by counting them, releaseOthers reports what it released, BOTH renderers release before they acquire asserted from source by comparing the two positions, and the rAF fallback exists. 23 plus 02 plus 09 plus 08: 43 passed, 1 skipped. THE .427 HAND-BACK IS UNDISTURBED - the ten-round-trip trace is byte-identical to before this ship, one live context on every round. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, CSS braces balanced, CRLF intact, three-stamp lockstep. No UI change, no CSS change. ?legacy=1 unaffected - the single-context guard was already deliberately ungated in both houses and this only reorders when it runs. DEVICE-VERIFY: this one wants hardware. Verify items 3 and 4 - the rack holds in Build across ten Tools round trips, and Open Aisle then close returns to Build with the rack still there, ten times. Watch for any added hitch on the handoff: two frames should be imperceptible, and if the aisle feels slower to open that is the finding.
